implementation_notes: The package is the pattern's canonical implementation: one Group per class of work, and Do(key, fn) guarantees a single in-flight execution per key while duplicates block and receive the same val/err, with a shared flag that reports whether the value went to more than one caller. The group removes the key automatically when the call finishes, so nothing is cached for later callers; Forget(key) drops an in-flight key so the next call re-executes instead of joining. When a caller must not block - request handlers with contexts and deadlines - use DoChan plus a select on ctx.Done(): the caller abandons the wait while the shared flight continues for the others.
pitfalls: Do blocks the caller, so a request that must respect a deadline needs DoChan plus a select on ctx.Done(); the flight keeps running after the waiter abandons it.
Key by every result-affecting input, tenant and authorisation scope included: a Group keyed by user id alone will coalesce across principals.
fn must not call Do with the same key - the caller would wait on its own flight - so recursive reuse needs distinct keys.
A panic inside fn is re-panicked to the waiters rather than returned as an error, and the key is removed afterwards; recover at the worker boundary, not inside Do.
A stuck call inside fn blocks every joiner until it returns, and the key is only forgotten when the call returns - bound the work inside fn.
Group is a namespace, not a cache: results for later callers do not exist by design; wrap a real cache around it when reuse is needed.
